title: Fire suppression in the data hall
alt: A section through a data hall and its valve room. Sprinkler pipes and a thin air-sampling pipe run along the ceiling over a row of racks. Smoke rises from one rack and is drawn along the sampling pipe to a detector on the wall, which flashes; water rises from the valve room and fills the sprinkler pipes; one head over the burning rack sprays while the others stay shut.
sources: project decision: data hall sprinklered, pre-action

air-sampling pipe, sampling holes and detector unit

steps.caption: The data hall has sprinklers, but the pipes hold air, not water.
So a broken pipe or a knocked head can't spray the servers.
If a rack catches fire, air-sampling detectors sense the smoke early.
Water is let into the pipes only when a detector and a sprinkler head have both gone off.
Only the head heated by the fire sprays; the others stay shut.

camera: face-on section; slides from the hall to the detector, the valve room and the burning rack, then pulls back
